newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares stay on course to record high.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares stay on course to record high.

text.p: Egyptian share prices continued on Thursday ascending to their highest level in about two years, with milling shares among the most active performers.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) overall index rose 0.44 points to 239.96 points, its highest level since early December 1994. Volume reached 18.76 million pounds ($5.5 million).
One broker said the market was relatively quiet with some problems lingering over a new computerised clearing system.
"But even though this is happening, the prices have gone up. People are willing to go into the market and buy those (milling and cement) shares," the broker said.

General Silos and Storage shares worth 3.0 million pounds changed hands and brokers attributed the volume to transfers of shares to the firm's workers unions as part of its recent privatisation. Shares ended unchanged at 39.00 pounds.
Milling shares were among the top six in terms of turnover.
Central and West Delta Flour Mills shares worth 1.47 million pounds were traded, closing down 0.01 at 58.65 pounds in its second consecutive day of strong activity.
Upper Egypt Flour Mills shares also crossed the mark to 1.06 million pounds, ending 0.50 lower at 48.20 pounds.

Family Foods was the day's biggest gainer, with one move boosting the share value 9.68 percent to close at 272 pounds. The broker said Family Foods is mainly owned by large investors who trade among themselves.
The CMA index for openly traded firms rose to 359.68 points from 359.47 on Wednesday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 169.08 from 168.66 points.
Advances outnumbered declines 29 to 19, while 23 shares ended unchanged.
